claims.text: Sialon-based ceramics can be used as molten-aluminum-contact components such as rollers and guide plates in hot-dip aluminum plating lines.
Sialon-based ceramic components will exhibit superior corrosion resistance to molten aluminum.
Using sialon-based ceramic contact components will extend equipment service life.
The proposed components consist of sialon-based ceramic sintered and machined to the required shape and surface finish.
The intended operating environment is continuous or extended immersion in molten aluminum at approximately 650–750°C.
The sialon material has a dense matrix.
The sialon matrix contains stable Si-O-N bonds.
Sialon ceramics resist wetting by molten aluminum.
Resistance to molten-aluminum wetting minimizes corrosive reactions and chemical dissolution.
Sialon ceramics undergo less corrosive reaction and chemical dissolution in molten aluminum than conventional steel or Ni-based components.
Molten-aluminum exposure will produce reduced mass loss in sialon ceramic relative to standard metallic parts.
Sialon components will exhibit negligible structural deterioration during molten-aluminum exposure.
Sialon components will have a longer lifetime than standard metallic components under the same molten-aluminum conditions.
The proposed use is limited to moderate mechanical loading and temperatures of approximately 650–750°C.
